source_snapshot.items: AMD GPU RAS tool version check
source_snapshot.procedure: If required, install an approved amdgpuras package for the target OS; run source command `sudo amdgpuras -v`; collect raw output and unexpected logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Reported version is equal to or newer than1.6.3.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES but changes -v to --version and overlooks package mutation.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC because install provenance/rollback need approval, while query and threshold are defined.

old_problem: The review treated approved package provenance, OS compatibility, install/rollback and version-suffix policy as an unresolved engineering decision despite a complete minimum-version oracle.
disposition_reason: ED-03 and the parameterization rule allow package artifact, OS and rollback to be Runtime Project Configuration. The source gives an exact read-only query and authoritative minimum1.6.3; no OEM command semantics or hardware PASS evidence is missing. Installation remains separately authorized, but Review-layer acceptance is complete.
decision_basis: Directly read all18 XLSX cells and history2571.
Preserved source `-v` command, >=1.6.3 threshold, install step, results and unexpected-log collection.
Did not assume `--version` alias or an unapproved latest package; pinned artifact/signature are runtime inputs.
No package installation or DUT command occurred.

test_case.test_name: Parameterized AMDGPU-RAS approved package and minimum-version check
test_case.purpose: Confirm the installed approved amdgpuras build reports a version at least1.6.3 before any GPU RAS test.
required_package: Package-manager authorization and previous-version rollback artifact
Documented suffix comparison policy for the approved build
test_case.test_command: Record current package/tool state. If absent or below policy, install only the approved artifact under change control. Run the literal source command `sudo amdgpuras -v`, preserving stdout, stderr and exit code; parse the numeric version under the approved suffix policy and compare it with1.6.3. Do not inject any error.
test_case.expected_result: The command exits successfully and reports an authenticated installed build whose normalized version is >=1.6.3; package metadata matches the approved artifact and no unexpected driver/package error is introduced.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires approved artifact identity, successful raw `-v` output and semantic version >=1.6.3. Missing/unapproved package, unparsable or prerelease-disallowed version, nonzero exit, version below minimum or unhealthy package/driver state fails. Hardware behavior is not claimed.
safety_gate: Query existing tool before any package mutation.
Install only a signed/hash-approved target-OS artifact with explicit change authorization.
Preserve current package state and rollback artifact before upgrade.
No GPU injection, driver reset or reboot is part of this case.
expected_evidence: Approved package source/hash/signature and install authorization if used
test_case.recovery: If installation or health verification fails, preserve logs and roll back to the captured previous package using the approved package-manager procedure; do not continue to RAS injection tests until health is restored.

source_conflict.reason: Procedure and criterion consistently define a minimum-version check; `latest` is replaced by an approved pinned runtime artifact without reducing coverage.

blocked.reason: The query and acceptance are complete; artifact/OS/rollback are runtime configuration rather than a missing core engineering decision.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: At execution time bind target OS/architecture/driver, approved package source/hash/signature, install authorization, suffix policy and rollback artifact.
pending.owner: Project package/release owner supplies runtime binding; test engineer captures evidence.
pending.unlock_condition: No review decision remains; execute only after runtime package/change-control prerequisites are satisfied.

project_authority: Project release authority selects the signed package and suffix policy; these are runtime bindings, not grounds for continued Review Pending.
